correctness.rationale: For both standard filiform brackets over F_q and n>=6, Jacobi follows because the e3..en ideal is abelian and ad_e1 and ad_e2 act by commuting shifts, including characteristic 2. For L: if a1 !=0 ad has rank n-2; else all brackets except ad(e1) vanish, giving rank1 for noncentral and rank0 for q central elements. Thus counts q, q^(n-1)-q, (q-1)q^(n-1). For M: a1 !=0 gives triangular rank n-2; a1=0,a2 !=0 yields e5..en plus independent e3 => rank n-3; a1=a2=0 gives rank2 iff some a3..a_(n-2) !=0, rank1 iff only a_(n-1) !=0, else rank0. Counts respectively q^(n-2)-q^2, q(q-1), q. All strata sum q^n; rank-nullity gives d_L=q^-2+(q^2-1)q^-n and d_M=q^-4+2(q^2-1)q^-n, difference (q^2-1)(q^(n-4)-1)/q^n>0. Independently built finite-field adjoint matrices and row-reduced for (q,n)=(2,6),(3,6), obtaining L counts [2,30,32], [3,240,486] and M [2,2,12,16,32], [3,6,72,162,486], consistent with universal symbolic strata; finite enumeration not proof.

originality.rationale: The original 2024 Shamsaki Example 3.8 already computes d for n=5 L-type and supplies universal averaging lemma, while the published Resultary almost-abelian theorem FULLY subsumes the L_n(q) rank spectrum for all n: L_n has abelian codim-one ideal span(e2..en), with operator rank n-2. This is explicitly acknowledged, not marketed as novel. However M_n(q) for n>=6 has no abelian codim-one ideal (any such ideal contains [M,M]=span(e3..en) but any complementary vector a e1+b e2 must have a=0 by bracket with e_(n-1), then b=0 by bracket with e3). The almost-abelian theorem cannot apply, nor does Shamsaki class-three derived-two paper for n>=6; new M-spectrum and provably strict separation remain an independent original mathematical claim in the joint theorem.
residual_risks: The L-family half of the joint claim is demonstrably covered by a broader published Resultary almost-abelian theorem; do not present it as new.
